h1:
Hat Yai Food & Shopping Itinerary
Dim Sum · Kim Yong · Night Markets
intro: Hat Yai is one of those cities where you can roll out of bed and immediately start eating. Mornings are for dim sum, midday is for browsing Kim Yong Market and loading up on souvenirs, and evenings bring a sprawling night market. We've put this plan together as tightly scheduled block days — no backtracking — with real restaurants, real opening hours, and rough prices. Works just as well for a 2-day trip or a 3-day one; just drop Day 3 if needed.

blocks.html: What makes Hat Yai so easy to explore is how close everything is. The city centre is walkable, and most of the famous spots sit within a few hundred metres of each other. The three things you really need to do: dim sum in the morning (a genuine daily ritual for locals here), Kim Yong Market for imported snacks and souvenirs at prices you won't find elsewhere, and a night market for a long, leisurely evening of eating.

blocks.text: Hat Yai Dim Sum — Where Locals Actually Go

blocks.html: Dim sum culture here runs deep — it came with the city's Sino-Thai community and never left. Baskets start around ฿15–30, so ordering several to share barely dents your wallet. These are the places that keep coming up in conversation and are still open.

items.name: Kuk Chai Dim Sum
items.blurb: A Hat Yai institution. Both locals and foreign visitors pack this place — siu mai, har gow, and bao all made fresh, same flavour as always. Expect a queue on weekend mornings.

items.name: Chok Dee Dim Sum (Chok Dee Tae Tiam)
items.blurb: A legendary spot in the city centre. Generous portions, low prices, and goes well alongside a bowl of hot bak kut teh — many regulars order both. Simple old-school Chinese shop-house feel.

items.name: Betong Dim Sum
items.blurb: Genuine Betong style — larger pieces, strong on prawn har gow and pork siu mai. Good with a hot tea. Worth trying if you want southern deep-south dim sum rather than the standard.

items.name: Hatyai Dimsum
items.blurb: Wider menu and slightly longer hours than most. Mon–Fri 07:00–14:00, Sat–Sun until 15:00. Good option if you're a late riser who still wants dim sum as a proper lunch.

items.name: Ah Ma Dim Sum
items.blurb: Newer fit-out, air-conditioned, comfortable seating — good for families or bigger groups. The food is solid and the space is clean if you're not used to the older-style shops.

items.name: Suan Siri Dim Sum
items.blurb: Traditional flavours, lots of regulars, good value. One order and you're full. The kind of place nearby workers stop at before heading to the office.

blocks.title: Dim Sum Tips
blocks.html: Popular places often sell out before noon — aim to arrive before 9:00 if you want the full menu · Order a few baskets at a time; they're small but filling fast · A glass of kopi (Thai-style old-school coffee) or iced barley pairs perfectly with dim sum here

blocks.text: Kim Yong Market — Souvenirs & Imported Goods

blocks.html: Kim Yong Market sits on Suphasarnrangsan Road, right in the middle of Hat Yai. It's a two-storey covered market that runs from morning until evening. The ground floor is all food — snacks, souvenirs, nuts, dried fruits, teas, and coffees. Upstairs: electronics, games, clothes, and imported goods from Malaysia and Indonesia. Prices are usually better than the malls, and you can bargain.

items: Malaysian imported snacks — chocolates, biscuits, sweets, and brands you won't easily find in Bangkok. Cheap and easy to carry.
Nuts and dried fruits — premium imported varieties, priced per kilo and cheaper than supermarkets. Most stalls let you taste before you buy.
Coffee and tea — southern kopi blends, instant iced-tea sachets. Popular, light, and easy to pack as gifts.
Processed seafood — dried squid, salted fish, quality shrimp paste. Look for vacuum-sealed packs if you're carrying them on a plane.
Phi Khong's Shop — a well-recommended souvenir stall inside the market, known for freshness and tight sealing. A safe bet for buying gifts.

blocks.title: Shopping Kim Yong Smarter
blocks.html: Walk two or three stalls and compare prices before buying — the same items vary more than you'd think · If you're buying several things from one vendor, ask for a small discount; most are happy to deal · Save heavy items like canned goods or bottles for your last stop of the day so you're not hauling them around for hours

blocks.text: Hat Yai Souvenirs Worth Bringing Home

blocks.html: Beyond Kim Yong, Hat Yai has a few iconic edible souvenirs sold at shops around the city. These are the ones people actually carry back on a regular basis.

items.name: Baan Ko Khai Bakery
items.blurb: Fresh-baked cakes and pastries made daily, no preservatives, halal certified. Multiple branches around the city including near Greenway — easy to grab on your way back.

items.name: Hat Yai Fried Chicken Sauce
items.blurb: Bottled to take home — the sweet-tangy-spicy southern dipping sauce that makes Hat Yai fried chicken what it is. Works with almost anything and it's a gift people don't usually see coming.

items.name: Hat Yai-Style Crispy Fried Shallots
items.blurb: Fried fresh before packing, good shelf life, and great sprinkled over rice, noodles, or eggs. A gift that travels well and tends to go over well with northern and central Thai friends.

blocks.text: Hat Yai Night Markets — Eating After Dark

blocks.html: Once the sun goes down, Hat Yai shifts into evening eating mode. There are a few markets to choose from depending on the day — Greenway is the biggest with the widest food selection, while Asean Night Bazaar is right in the city centre and walkable from most hotels.

items.name: Greenway Night Market
items.blurb: The biggest night market in town. Southern Thai food, international options, desserts, plus a full section of clothes, accessories, bags, and shoes. Open Tue–Sat 17:00–22:00. Better with a group.

items.name: Asean Night Bazaar
items.blurb: Right in the city centre — walkable from hotels in the Niphat Uthit area. Food, toys, clothes, all at low prices. Good for an after-dinner stroll without needing a car.

items.name: PSU Hat Yai Agriculture Market
items.blurb: Fresh produce, organic veg and fruit mixed with fusion food stalls and snacks. Student-crowd atmosphere, wallet-friendly prices. Go here if you want a market that feels genuinely local.

blocks.title: Before You Head to the Night Market
blocks.html: Check days in advance — Greenway is typically closed some days (usually Tue–Sat only) · Bring cash in small bills; many small stalls don't accept transfers · Arriving around 18:00 means the stalls are still fully stocked and it's not yet as crowded as it gets around 20:00

This plan keeps your days linear — no unnecessary backtracking. The goal is to eat well and shop smart without exhausting yourself. If you only have 2 days, drop Day 3 and squeeze the last round of souvenir shopping into Day 2 morning.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Morning Dim Sum + Kim Yong Market + Greenway Night Market

items.activity: Start the day with dim sum at Kuk Chai or Chok Dee
items.note: Get there before 9:00 to avoid the queue — order several baskets to share
Let breakfast settle before heading into shopping mode

items.activity: Browse Kim Yong Market for souvenirs
items.note: Compare a few stalls before buying; save heavy items for your last pass

items.activity: Southern Thai lunch in the city — rice and curry
items.note: Try kaeng luang (yellow curry) or bai liang stir-fry with egg — the real local stuff

items.activity: Back to the hotel to rest
items.note: Save your energy for the evening

items.activity: Head to Greenway Night Market for a long evening of eating
items.note: Open Tue–Sat — if it's a day off, swap to Asean Night Bazaar instead

items.activity: Dim sum at a new spot or a simple congee breakfast
items.note: Try Ah Ma Dim Sum if you want somewhere comfortable and air-conditioned
Walk around and catch the street art between stops

items.activity: Hat Yai fried chicken for lunch — try Decha
items.note: City branch opens 11:00–22:00; eat it with sticky rice

items.activity: Second souvenir run — Ko Khai bakery + crispy shallots + dipping sauce
items.note: Pick up anything you missed at Kim Yong the day before

items.activity: Asean Night Bazaar in the city centre
items.note: Walking distance from most hotels — cap the night with something sweet

blocks.title: Morning Market + Final Souvenir Run Before Heading Home

items.activity: Last dim sum session or a morning congee
items.note: Pick something close to your hotel so there's no rush

items.activity: PSU Agriculture Market or a fresh local market
items.note: Pick up fresh southern fruit to take with you

items.activity: Grab anything left on the souvenir list + check out

items.note: Allow buffer time to reach the airport or train station

items: The city centre is walkable — dim sum spots, Kim Yong Market, and Asean Night Bazaar are all in the same area and easy to reach on foot.
Greenway is slightly outside the centre — a motorbike taxi or Grab ride costs a matter of tens of baht.
Food budget per day — around ฿250–400/person if you're sticking to street food and dim sum.
Souvenir budget — ฿500–1,500 will fill a bag. Factor in some room for bargaining on top of that.
Cash — keep small bills on hand; markets and small stalls often prefer cash over transfers.

faq.q: Which Hat Yai dim sum restaurants open early and are worth visiting?
faq.a: Kuk Chai and Chok Dee Dim Sum are the two names that keep coming up — both are long-standing spots that open early. If you sleep in, Hatyai Dimsum stays open until 14:00 on weekdays and 15:00 on weekends. Most places start baskets at around ฿15–30. Get there before 9:00 at the popular spots, as they sell out fast.

faq.q: When does Kim Yong Market open and what should I buy there?
faq.a: It runs from morning until evening. The most popular buys are Malaysian imported snacks, nuts and dried fruit, southern Thai coffee and tea blends, and processed seafood. Prices tend to be lower than supermarkets and you can usually bargain — compare two or three stalls before committing.

faq.q: Which days are Hat Yai night markets open?
faq.a: Greenway Night Market is typically open Tuesday–Saturday, 17:00–22:00. If Greenway is closed on your night, Asean Night Bazaar in the city centre is open daily and walkable from most hotels. Always check current schedules before you go.

faq.q: Is 2 days enough in Hat Yai for food and shopping?
faq.a: Enough for the main highlights — morning dim sum, a proper Kim Yong shopping session, and one or two evenings at a night market. A third day lets you add the morning market and do a final souvenir sweep at a relaxed pace without feeling rushed.

faq.q: What are the best souvenirs to bring back from Hat Yai?
faq.a: The things people carry back most often: Baan Ko Khai fresh-baked pastries, bottled Hat Yai fried chicken dipping sauce, crispy fried shallots, and snacks or nuts from Kim Yong Market. Buy refrigerated or sealed items last, right before heading to the airport or station.
